the hydroboration of olefins and alkynes with the sodium borohydrides catalyzed by the Cp2TiCl 2 /NaBH4 /crown ether system in tetrahydrofuran (THF) is a very useful method for preparing alcohols and alkynes from the respective alkyl- and vinylboronates.
The reaction is catalyzed by a titanium complex prepared in situ from Cp2Ti(THF)2 and NaBH 4 in the presence of a crown ether, and the catalytic activity is dependent on the crown ether.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel and efficient catalytic methods for the hydroboration of unsaturated organic compounds.
the development of novel catalytic systems for the hydroboration of unsaturated hydrocarbons with sodium borohydroxide and sodium borohydrides.
the development of new synthetic methods for the selective functionalization of organic compounds, particularly the development of novel catalytic reactions using transition metal complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the catalytic hydroborations with sodium borohydride catalyzed by the titanium complex are highly regio- and stereoselective and proceed under very mild reaction conditions.
the catalytic hydroborations of alkenes with NaBH4 catalyzed by Cp2TiCl4 and NaBH4 are not only the first catalytic hydrobora- tion of alkenes but also the first catalytic reaction of NaBH4.

the hydroboration of olefins with sodium borohydrate catalyzed by a titanium complex prepared from NaBH4 and Cp2TiCl in the presence of a suitable crown ether is a convenient, mild, and selective method for the preparation of primary alcohols from olefins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydroboration of olefins and alkynes can be carried out in a catalytic manner with the sodium borohydrides as the boron source and the titanium complex as the catalyst.
the catalytic hydrocarbon of alkene and alkyne with sodium borohydrate is achieved by the combination of the sodium borohydraide with the Cp2TiCl 2.

we developed a novel catalytic hydroborylation of alkenes, alkynes, and allenes with sodium borohydroide catalyzed by the titanium complex prepared from NaBH4 and Cp2TiCl4 in the presence of 18-crown-6.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a crown ether in this system is critical for catalytic hydroborage to occur.
the hydroboration of alkynes is possible under mild conditions with a simple and inexpensive catalyst.
